A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a family of parallel sorting algorithms that, for any fixed value of α, have a performance that is asymptotically the same as Hirschberg's algorithm, but are free of memory fetch conflicts.

, for a multiprocess system, the algorithms described here provide an alternative to Hirschberg's algorithm and are free of fetch conflicts; in addition, they can be used to sort a set of keys with a processor set of smaller cardinality than that required by Hirschberg's algorithms.
, for a multiprocessorsystem, we present an algorithm that sorts n keys in time C logn + o(logn) using n1 + α processors, where C is a constant and α is a small constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of parallel merge algorithms to implement the count acquisition phase can lead to a significant improvement of the sorting performance.
the parallel-merging technique is useful in sorting algorithms and that parallel sorting algorithms can be designed by using the merging technique in a natural manner.
the performance of the parallel-sorting algorithms is not necessarily determined by the time required for the data rearrangement phase, as has been the case with most parallel sorting schemes.
